sources.note: The awarding body's own page for the programme (European Society of Cardiology site, Education > Career Development > Grants). Read in full on 12 October 2026.

Programme Conditions and Regulations on the same escardio.org domain, reached from the main programme page. Restates the eligibility criteria, the annual application window, the payment schedule and the relocation exclusion.
ESC 'Training Grants and Fellowships' index, which lists this programme alongside the other ESC association grants. No application dates given.

Read only to check the awarding body's base location. States two administrative centres: the European Heart House in Sophia Antipolis, France, and a Brussels office in Belgium. No Swiss office is listed.

awarding_body.detail: The page is the awarding body's own: it sits on escardio.org under Education > Career Development > Grants and is titled 'HFA Research and Training Grants Programme'. The HFA is the Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology, listed in the ESC's own navigation as an association ('HFA: Heart failure'). It is not a news article, student blog, aggregator or Wikipedia mirror.
awarding_body.quote: The HFA provides grants up to €10,000 to help young members undertake specialised heart failure research or training in an ESC member country outside their own country.

deadline.detail: The page confirms the record's 30 September deadline and its 10 April - 30 September window, but states no year. The 2026 window closed on 30 September 2026, twelve days before this check on 12 October 2026, and the programme runs annually, so the campaign is between cycles: the record cannot be shown to describe a currently-open cycle. The next window would be expected to open on 10 April 2027, but the page does not state a 2027 date.
deadline.quote: The online application form must be submitted between 10 April and 30 September each year.

eligibility.detail: Every distinct claim in the record's summary is confirmed by the Conditions and Regulations: under 40; HFA Member or Fellow; an MD without yet holding a 'permanent', 'senior staff' or 'consultant' post, with demonstrated heart failure expertise, OR a PhD/DPhil or a submitted thesis; and a project in an ESC member country other than the applicant's own for a minimum of three months. One material item is missing from the record's summary: selection also awards 20% for 'Citizenship or permanent residence in a low/middle-income country as defined by the World Bank', which narrows the realistic applicant pool well beyond what the record states.
eligibility.quote:
Applicants should fulfil the following conditions as of the application deadline:
2.1 Be under 40 years old at the day of application deadline
2.2 Be an HFA Member, or Fellow of the HFA
2.3 Hold a MD but have not yet obtained a post defined as 'permanent', 'senior staff' or 'consultant' and be able to demonstrate expertise in Heart Failure through examination, practice, scientific publication in a relevant journal or abstract presentation at a national or international meeting; OR
2.4 Hold a PhD, DPhil degree or equivalent, or have submitted a thesis before starting the research period relating to the grant.

funding.detail: The record's 'Partially Funded' is correct. The award is a stipend of €2,500 per month, capped at €10,000, for a research or training exchange of three to twelve months in a host centre. It is not tuition support and explicitly excludes relocation: 'The ESC will not provide assistance with transfer or household removal expenses incurred by grant recipients on taking up an award.' This is a partial award by any reading, not a fully funded one.
funding.quote: HFA Grant recipients will receive €2,500 per month with a maximum of €10,000 according to the length of the project.

degree_levels.detail: The page states no degree level and the award confers no degree. It funds a research or training exchange of three to twelve months, normally administered through a fixed-term contract of employment with the host institution. The target audience is early-career, which is broadly consistent with the record's 'Postdoctoral' label, but the label itself appears nowhere on the page and is an editorial inference rather than a published claim.
degree_levels.quote: The HFA Grants programme enable medical and science graduates, who have completed the major part of their cardiology training but have not yet obtained a permanent status, to undertake specialised heart failure research or training in an ESC Member Country, outside their own country.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Application period is 10 April to 30 September. The online application form must be submitted between 10 April and 30 September each year.
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Official pages read on 12 October 2026 and both are live and consistent. The programme's wording, eligibility criteria, funding amount and awarding body all agree with the record. Two things block an 'active' verdict. (1) The application window runs 10 April - 30 September every year and the 2026 window closed on 30 September 2026, twelve days before this check, so the record describes a closed cycle and must not be presented to users as currently accepting applications; re-check from 10 April 2027. (2) The page publishes no degree level and the award is a 3-12 month research/training exchange, not a degree, so the 'Postdoctoral' degree-level label cannot be confirmed from the source. Also worth carrying forward: the record's eligibility summary omits the 20% selection weight for 'Citizenship or permanent residence in a low/middle-income country as defined by the World Bank', which materially narrows the pool; and the record's country 'Switzerland' does not match the awarding body, whose own offices page lists the European Heart House in Sophia Antipolis, France and a Brussels office in Belgium.

notes_for_reviewer: A human should decide three things. (a) The record's deadline_date of 2026-09-30 is now past; the page gives a recurring annual window with no year, so the date should either be refreshed to the next window (expected 10 April - 30 September 2027, which the page does not state) or the record should be marked as closed until April 2027. (b) The eligibility summary should be extended with the World Bank low/middle-income country selection criterion, otherwise the record promises eligibility to applicants who will not be competitive. (c) The country field says Switzerland, but the ESC is headquartered in Sophia Antipolis, France with a Brussels office in Belgium - 'Multiple' or 'Europe' is more accurate. The country field is outside the five checks this campaign requires, so it is reported here rather than being used to drive the verdict.
